_comment: L2.e' of docs/2026-09-07_latent_intent_design.zh.md: the warm posterior's next two rungs. L2.d (l2_warm_posterior_20260907) at beta 0.01 kept z alive to the end (active_units 2.82, 0.17 nats/flight at the best epoch 175) and is the best point estimate so far (top-1 ADE 1214 vs native32's 1322, 65 % paired win, vectored -227 m, bank skill 0.729), but gates (1) and (2) still fail: z carries only 0.17 nats and six samples from the trained prior lose to six N(0, I) draws (1004 vs 947 m minADE_6) — the prior is NARROWER than N(0, I), i.e. the decoder's z-direction is meaningful beyond the trained range and q/p are simply compressed. The units say why: at beta 0.01 a nat still costs 0.01 loss units, above the whole 0.009 the position term could pay, so z can only earn through the imitation term. Same base as L2.d (warm posterior q-std 0.1, K=1, N=32, simple-v3 supervision + teacher, free bits 0.05/dim), full 180 epochs (the erosion dynamics are slow; a 60-epoch screen cannot see them); arms differ only in beta: 0.001 and 0.0001. READOUT as L2.d, plus the z-oracle (a predict-only arms file in the shape of l2d_zoracle_arms.json). PRE-REGISTERED READING: (a) the autoencoder form appears (top-1 worse than native32, z-oracle excellent) -> take the largest beta still passing gate (3) — beta 0.01 is already the fallback winner; (b) z still carries < 1 nat at 0.001 -> the price is not beta but the position term's units (position_loss_scale_m), change that next, not beta; (c) gates (1)(2) pass -> carry that beta to K=4 and to L3. Gates and veto as before; gate (3) of the z-oracle (vectored <= 1235 m) read on every arm.
